It is read-only and non-owning: nothing is persisted, no date is editable from this view, and a Project or Milestone with no dates simply does not render a bar.
features.useCase: PM ดู Project และ Milestone บน timeline แบบ global หรือ project-scoped โดยไม่เขียนวันที่จากหน้านี้

features.title: Import target authorization: the FR-012 pipeline authorizes the Workspace it is about to write to, instead of accepting whichever `workspaceId` the request body names. All three intake routes (`/api/import/dry-run`, `/api/import/commit`, `/api/import/xlsx`) resolve a viewer, and the target Workspace is resolved **before** validation so an unauthorized target is refused without the caller learning anything about the plan. (a) A **Business-scoped** Workspace requires `ownsBusiness(viewer, workspace.businessId)` — the same predicate the other write paths use, not a second reading of it; a caller who may see the Business but does not own it is refused. (b) A Workspace **above Business** (`scopeType` PORTFOLIO or TENANT) is refused with an explicit reason stating that no authority above Business is declared — this requirement deliberately does **not** invent one. Enabling such an import requires a prior FR that makes portfolio/tenant authority *holdable*: a viewer-contract change in the manner of FR-061, since today no principal can hold it. The dry run is authorized identically to the commit — a read-only preview of another scope's contents is the leak the commit guard would otherwise still allow.
features.useCase: ระบบตรวจสิทธิ์ Workspace ก่อน dry-run หรือ commit แผนที่ผู้ใช้นำเข้า

features.title: Profile-first onboarding: after a provider-neutral local identity/session exists, every new person completes a Profile before being asked to create or select operating scope. A Profile-only member may remain in Waiting Room without creating Organization/Tenant, Business, Space or Project; an owner may create a top-level Workspace and add those scopes only when needed. Profile is not an authorization grant. Waiting Room renders only the current person's completed Profile summary and provides an accessible action back to public Home.
features.useCase: สมาชิกใหม่สร้าง Profile และอยู่ Waiting Room ได้โดยยังไม่ต้องสร้าง Business หรือ Project

features.title: Workspace collaboration boundary: an authorized Workspace/Tenant owner can issue a scoped, expiring, single-use invite that creates a separate WorkspaceMembership. Workspace membership grants only Workspace collaboration visibility; Tenant, Business, Space and Project access require separate server-authorized assignment, with audit and fail-closed replay/revocation behavior.
features.useCase: Workspace owner ส่ง invite แบบหมดอายุและใช้ครั้งเดียวโดยไม่ให้สิทธิ์ Business อัตโนมัติ

features.title: Supabase data pipeline monitor and replay: the governed SmartGift DuckDB/source-artifact → Supabase pipeline exposes stable definition, run, stage, step, attempt, record, batch, `doc_id`, `pic_id`, `fact_id`, destination and audit IDs, plus the complete supporting identity envelope (`node_id`, `edge_id`, `artifact_id`, `contract_id` (CRM Contact), `meeting_id`, `call_id`, `followup_id`, `req_id`, `verify_id`, `gate_id`, `integration_id`, `graph_id`, `workflow_contract_id`, `workflow_id`, `runbook_id`, `promotion_id`, `skill_id`, `tool_id`) on every stage/record event; monitors hashes/counts/status/tags/failure points; and supports authorized full, failed-stage, failed-record and provenance-filtered replay with immutable lineage, scope checks, RLS and idempotent destination writes.
features.useCase: Operator ดู pipeline stage ที่ล้มแล้ว replay เฉพาะ record นั้นโดยรักษา lineage และ idempotency

features.title: Project-Manager mutation authorization: every mutating route repaid from `docs/.route-viewer-baseline.json` resolves a request viewer and the service behind it refuses the write unless `ownsBusiness(viewer, <governing Business>)`, where the governing Business is derived from the target's Space (`workspace.businessId`; for Project-scoped targets via the Project's Space per FR-043; for a Dependency, the governing Business of **both** endpoints; for a Project moved between Spaces, the authority of **both** the current governing Business and the destination Space). (a) A Business-governed target that is not owned answers exactly as a nonexistent one, so a refusal is never an enumeration oracle over another tenant's ids. (b) A target governed above Business (a Project in a PORTFOLIO/TENANT Space, a non-BUSINESS-scoped Workspace) is refused for **every** principal with a reason naming the missing authority — this requirement deliberately does **not** invent authority above Business; enabling such writes requires a prior FR that makes that authority holdable (FR-066/FR-067 direction), per the FR-065 precedent. Routes whose authorization question no declared rule answers (`/api/scope`, `/api/backup/import`) are out of scope and remain recorded debt in `docs/.route-viewer-baseline.json`, each with the missing decision named. (`/api/repositories` and `/api/repositories/[id]` were answered by FR-073 and repaid.)
features.useCase: mutating route ปฏิเสธการแก้ Project หรือ dependency เมื่อ viewer ไม่ได้เป็นเจ้าของ Business ที่เกี่ยวข้อง

features.title: Repository ownership: a `Repository` is owned by exactly one Business (`Repository.businessId`), which is the decision FR-072 recorded as missing for `/api/repositories` and `/api/repositories/[id]`. Business rather than Tenant or Portfolio is forced, not chosen: the viewer contract carries only Business-keyed grants, so no principal can hold authority above Business (SDD-037) and a higher-scoped Repository would be ungovernable. (a) Creating a Repository requires `ownsBusiness(viewer, businessId)`, and the Business is required at the input boundary so every new Repository is governed. (b) Updating one requires the same authority over its owning Business; an unowned Repository answers exactly as a nonexistent one. (c) Linking a Repository to a Project requires authority over **both** the Project's governing Business and the Repository's Business — the same fail-closed composition FR-072 applies to a Dependency edge. (d) `Repository.businessId` is nullable only for rows predating this requirement; such a Repository is governed by nobody, is refused for every principal with the missing owner named, and is invisible to every reader until backfilled (`scripts/backfill-repository-business.mjs`, which infers an owner only where a Repository's Project links agree and reports the rest rather than guessing). (e) Listing Repositories is scoped by `seesBusiness`, closing a cross-tenant read that previously returned every Repository in the installation with its project links attached.
features.useCase: Owner สร้าง repository ใต้ Business และ link กับ Project เมื่อมีสิทธิ์ทั้งสองฝั่ง

features.title: Scope-creation authorization: every creator behind `POST /api/scope` resolves a viewer and is authorized at the scope it actually writes, in three tiers. (a) **Business scope** — `branch` and a BUSINESS-scoped `workspace` require `ownsBusiness(viewer, businessId)`. (b) **Tenant scope** — creating a `business` inside an existing Tenant, or a TENANT-scoped `workspace`, requires `ownsTenant(viewer, tenantId)`, surfaced on the viewer contract as `ownedTenantIds` from the tenant-wide OWNER Membership that already existed in the data and was previously only expanded into `ownedBusinessIds`. This names a held row; it grants nobody anything new, and is deliberately not satisfied by owning every Business in a Tenant. (c) **Self-service provisioning** — `businessInGroup` creates a new Tenant + Business + Workspace for any authenticated principal, because nothing exists to own beforehand, and **binds the creator as OWNER in the same transaction**. Without that binding the caller would provision scope they cannot subsequently write to, which is the defect this clause fixes as well as authorizes. `portfolio`, `tenant`, `legalEntity` and a PORTFOLIO-scoped `workspace` are installation primitives above any Tenant and require FR-075 operator authority. Self-service is never unauthenticated: the viewer is resolved, the write is attributed, and an audit event is recorded.
features.useCase: ระบบอนุญาตสร้าง Branch, Business หรือ Workspace ตาม authority tier ที่ตรงกับ scope จริง

features.title: Installation-operator authority: an installation-wide operation is authorized by a named capability, `isOperator`, carried on the viewer contract and true only for a server-held platform grant (FR-031, on a trusted session per SEC-008), and false for every ordinary authenticated principal however much of the installation they own. It governs `POST /api/backup/import` — both the preview and the restore, since a preview of every table across every tenant is the same disclosure the restore guard would otherwise still permit — and the scope primitives above any Tenant (FR-074). This is a distinct *scope* of authority rather than a larger amount of Business ownership: a restore replaces Portfolios, Tenants, identities and audit rows, so no composition of `ownsBusiness` can express it, which is why the route was unrepayable until the capability was named. `isPlatform` remains visibility-only and is never read as authority (RCA 2026-08-16).
features.useCase: installation operator preview และ restore snapshot โดย ordinary Business Owner ทำไม่ได้

features.title: Product Owner Business role binding: a Person may hold one active generic `RoleBinding` with `roleKey=PRODUCT_OWNER` per assigned Business inside a customer Tenant; the registry expands it only to Product permissions for that Business, never Business/Tenant/Workspace ownership, Resource/Operations, Marketing, Platform, Integration, secret, LINE or import authority. Bindings are trusted, Business-scoped, revocable, audited and fail closed.
features.useCase: ผู้ดูแลมอบ Product Owner role เฉพาะ Business โดยไม่ขยายสิทธิ์ Platform หรือ secret

features.title: Raw external ingestion boundary: every acquisition channel (webhook, pull, file, manual) converges on one normalized ingestion envelope carrying tenant, Business, connection, provider, lane, entity type, external id, source type and schema version, and a channel is added as an adapter rather than a second raw-write path. (a) Ingestion identity is `sha256(tenantId, connectionId, entityType, externalId, payloadHash)` over a canonically serialized payload, so a re-delivered event resolves to `UNCHANGED` instead of a duplicate row; the external id contributes to that identity and is never itself a key (BR-002). (b) Raw records are read and written only through a repository bound to one tenant/connection scope, which refuses a row outside it rather than filtering afterwards (SEC-001), and a referenced Business or IngestionRun must itself resolve inside that scope. (c) Raw ingestion persists the source payload verbatim and never writes domain truth: translation into business entities is a separate later path, so a failed translation cannot corrupt the evidence it was derived from. (d) A run records its own counts and terminal state, and a failure is preserved as a DeadLetterRecord naming the failing stage and owner rather than being retried silently. This requirement declares the ingestion substrate only; no scheduler, no translation ACL and no reader surface is in scope.
features.useCase: LINE event ถูกเก็บเป็น raw evidence แบบ idempotent ก่อน translation โดยตัด reply token ออก

features.title: Schema declaration for the live production-auth tables: `PersonCredential`, `PasswordResetToken` and `Workstream.laneId` exist on the Supabase database — `PersonCredential` with a real credential row and `laneId` with a distinct value on every Workstream — but existed in no committed schema, having been pushed there from the unmerged branch `codex/postgres-primary-runtime`. This requirement declares their shape so the schema describes the database that exists. It is deliberately **declaration only**: no service, route or UI is in scope, and the feature code remains on that branch. The reason it cannot wait for that branch to merge is that `prisma migrate diff` proposes `DROP TABLE "PersonCredential"` against an undeclared table, so any routine `db push` destroys a live credential without the operator reading the SQL. Registering the tables here removes the destructive suggestion without deciding the feature's fate. **Resolution (2026-08-26):** the branch was never merged and no longer needs to be — `main` grew its own superior implementations of everything it held (`PersonCredential` login/logout via FR-046/FR-095; password reset via FR-104, reimplemented rather than revived because the draft returned the raw reset token to the unauthenticated caller). Its FR-082/FR-083 claims stay burnt on the pipeline canvas. The branch is deleted; `Workstream.laneId` remains declared-only.
features.useCase: Operator เปรียบเทียบ schema โดยไม่ให้เครื่องมือเสนอ DROP ตาราง credential ที่มีอยู่จริง

features.title: Market translation core: an eligible Integration-owned `RawExternalRecord` is loaded through a trusted scoped read port and translated into one provider-neutral Market-owned `MarketObservation`. Source adapters may extract candidate fields but cannot author trusted scope/lineage. Canonical Product/Category resolution is delegated to governed Knowledge/GKS and unresolved identity remains a valid state.
features.useCase: ระบบแปล raw marketplace record เป็น MarketObservation พร้อม source lineage และ unresolved identity ที่ซื่อสัตย์

features.title: SoT data-plane service-account authentication: a `SotDataPlaneKey` bound to exactly one Tenant lets the SoT pipeline's external data plane authenticate to the FR-100 submit/export endpoints (`Authorization: Bearer sdpk_...`) without a browser session and without installation-operator authority. Revocation takes effect on the next request; the raw secret is never persisted, only its SHA-256 hash.
features.useCase: data plane ภายนอกของ SoT Pipeline ยิงเข้า submit/export ด้วย service-account key ที่ผูก Tenant เดียว โดยไม่ต้องมี browser session และเพิกถอนได้ทันทีในคำขอถัดไป

features.title: SEC-005 PDPA consent, MVP scope: a Business owner attests in the CRM console that a Customer's consent was captured (`GRANTED`/`DECLINED`), recorded with timestamp and attesting Person on the Customer row FR-023 already treats as the CRM-sharing unit. Every Customer created from here on defaults to `PENDING`; rows that predate this column backfill to `GRANDFATHERED` rather than being retroactively blocked. Closes ethics-governance.md's open question #4 only — it does not gate AI processing, redact model input, or answer retention/provider-terms (#1, #2, #3, #6), which stay open.
features.useCase: เจ้าของธุรกิจบันทึกในคอนโซล CRM ว่าลูกค้ารายนี้ให้หรือปฏิเสธ consent พร้อมเวลาและผู้บันทึก โดยแถวเดิมที่มีก่อนคอลัมน์นี้ไม่ถูกปิดกั้นย้อนหลัง

features.title: Owner-assisted password reset: a Business owner over a Business the target Person belongs to — the same authority boundary as FR-038 Membership administration — or the installation operator mints a single-use, one-hour, hash-bound reset token (`POST /api/platform/users/password-resets`), and the public `POST /api/auth/reset-password` consumes it: new `PersonCredential`, token burnt, **every active Session revoked**. The raw token appears exactly once, in the authenticated mint response, for out-of-band handover (LINE, in person); it is stored only as a SHA-256 digest and never logged or audited in any form. There is deliberately no public forgot-password route: with no mail transport, such a route either returns the token to the unauthenticated caller — an account-takeover primitive, which is what the abandoned FR-082 draft on `codex/postgres-primary-runtime` shipped and the reason it was not revived as-is — or returns nothing and resets nothing. Uses the `PasswordResetToken` table FR-090 declared (its `token` column now carries the digest).
features.useCase: เจ้าของธุรกิจออก reset token ใช้ครั้งเดียวอายุหนึ่งชั่วโมงให้สมาชิกที่ล็อกอินไม่ได้ และ session เดิมทั้งหมดถูกตัดเมื่อผู้ใช้ตั้งรหัสใหม่

features.title: Platform Programme Roadmap: `/control/roadmap` is an installation-operator-only, read-only projection of the submitted 24-week programme. It is deliberately outside BusinessShell and `DOMAINS`: there is no active Business, Tenant, Project or Workstream scope, and the surface must not be mistaken for a user's operational work. A missing viewer follows the entry boundary; a trusted viewer is admitted only by the named `isOperator` capability from FR-075 — never by `isPlatform`, role, Business/Tenant ownership or domain visibility. The board is a static plan snapshot re-projected from ROADMAP-ZURI-AI-24W-PROGRAM's own frontmatter and tables (currently v0.3.0, baseline 7d8c9d0), carrying the document's `draft` status. It makes no write, persists no progress, exposes no API and never turns commit activity into programme completion. Declared as FR-105 rather than the branch's original FR-094, which main's canonical IAM slice claimed first (AGENTS.md §18 — the later declaration renumbers).
features.useCase: installation operator เปิด /control/roadmap เพื่ออ่านแผนงาน 24 สัปดาห์ที่ส่งไว้ โดยอยู่นอก BusinessShell และไม่มี Business scope ใดปะปน

features.title: Enterprise API tenant token authentication: the FR-019 Enterprise API refuses every request that does not present a valid per-Tenant service-account key, generalizing the FR-102 pattern (ADR-047 D3 deliberately scoped its `SotDataPlaneKey` to the two SoT routes and named this generalization as the follow-up) rather than inventing a second mechanism: an `ApiAccessKey` bound to exactly one Tenant, presented as `Authorization: Bearer`, stored only as a SHA-256 digest, minted by an installation operator or an owner in that Tenant with the raw secret shown exactly once, revocable with effect on the next request, and never readable back. Scope on every request is the key's own Tenant — a key can never widen the ExternalRef/upsert surface beyond the Tenant it names (SEC-001, BR-002), and an invalid, revoked or missing key answers identically so the endpoint is not an enumeration oracle. This closes SEC-006, which has held the Enterprise API in a declared-but-unenforced state since ADR-047 recorded that "no API-key mechanism exists anywhere in zuri-ai".
features.useCase: ระบบภายนอกเรียก Enterprise API ด้วย ApiAccessKey ที่ผูก Tenant เดียว และคำขอที่ไม่มีกุญแจถูกปฏิเสธทั้งหมด

features.title: Installation-operator grant store and bootstrap: FR-075's `isOperator` capability becomes holdable in production. A `PlatformGrant` row (Person-bound, capability `OPERATOR`, revocable, audited) is the server-held store, and the session port resolves `platformGrant` from it on every request — replacing the hardcoded `false` that made the capability unholdable by any web session — so revoking a grant denies the very next request and no session snapshot outlives it (NFR-019 discipline). `scripts/bootstrap-operator.mjs` creates the installation's FIRST operator (Person + scrypt credential with a random initial password shown exactly once + ACTIVE grant, one transaction, audited with no password material) and refuses while any ACTIVE OPERATOR grant stands — bootstrap serves the empty operator set only; every later grant is issued by a standing operator. Where the store is absent (test doubles, pre-migration databases) resolution reads `false`, the pre-FR-107 behavior, never a widened one.
features.useCase: ผู้ดูแลมอบและเพิกถอนสิทธิ์ installation operator ให้ Person หนึ่งได้จริงในโปรดักชัน โดยทุกคำขออ่านสิทธิ์นั้นใหม่จาก grant store

features.title: Structural knowledge chunking with parent-child lineage: a parsed document is split along its own structure — document → section → chunk — rather than at a fixed token stride, and every chunk carries the eight fields FR-109's `DPS-KI-CHUNK` catalog row already fixes (`chunk_id`, `parent_id`, `document_id`, `sequence`, `heading_path`, `token_count`, `scope`, `provenance`). `heading_path` carries the whole ancestor chain rather than the nearest heading, so a chunk retrieved on its own still says where in the document it came from. A section too large to retrieve as one unit additionally gets overlapping fixed windows beneath it, parented to the section chunk and reported as a warning — the fallback the specification names (§12), never the default; the windows overlap because without it a sentence lying across a boundary is left whole in neither. Chunking derives nothing it is given: `scope` comes from FR-111 classification and `provenance` from Stage 3, both upstream. The function is pure — no I/O, no clock, no randomness — so the same document chunks to the same ids every time, which is what lets BR-021 treat a reprocessed document as the same knowledge rather than a duplicate. Stage 7 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.
features.useCase: เอกสารหนึ่งถูกแบ่งตามโครงสร้างของตัวเอง document → section → chunk โดยทุก chunk ยังบอกได้ว่ามาจากหัวข้อใดและลำดับที่เท่าไร

features.title: Entity candidate extraction from chunks and structured records: FR-112's chunks and caller-named record fields both yield `EntityCandidate` objects carrying the six fields FR-109's `DPS-KI-ENTITY-EXTRACT` catalog row fixes — `candidate_id`, type, mention, `normalized_name`, `source_chunk_id`, `confidence` — plus the originating chunk or record, the scope it was found in, and the provenance carried from that source so the chain back to the raw artifact survives, so a candidate can never be read outside its tenant (SEC-001, BR-001). A candidate is a mention with a guess attached and never an identity: the specification states it outright (§13, "EntityCandidate ยังไม่ใช่ canonical entity"), so two mentions of the same name stay two candidates and nothing here merges, links or resolves them — that judgement is Stage 9, which ADR-050 D2 and the specification both assign to GKS. Recognition is a seam with a deliberately narrow deterministic default (SDD-060); a record mention is read from a declared field rather than guessed, and carries confidence 1 for that reason. Pure — no I/O, no clock, no randomness, no model — so the same input yields the same candidate ids, which is what lets BR-021 treat a reprocessed document as the same knowledge. Stage 8 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.
features.useCase: ระบบดึง entity candidate จาก chunk และ record พร้อมค่า confidence และ chunk ต้นทาง เพื่อให้ตรวจย้อนกลับได้ว่าชื่อนี้มาจากตรงไหน

features.title: Canonical normalization that never destroys the raw value: a value is returned as the pair `{ raw, canonical }`, where `raw` is the input byte for byte and `canonical` is the comparable form — the specification's §3.1 invariant that raw data stays recoverable, made structural rather than promised, and the evidence FR-109's `DPS-KI-NORMALIZE` catalog row already asks for. Six categories are normalized: Unicode and whitespace (NFC, plus the invisible spaces `s` does not match, plus the one Thai fold NFC misses — `สำ` written as NIKHAHIT + SARA AA renders identically to SARA AM and NFC leaves the two unequal), dates (Thai and Gregorian digits, four-digit Buddhist years without a hint, two-digit years only with a declared era), Thai telephone numbers to E.164, email with the domain lowercased and the local part left alone because RFC 5321 makes it case-sensitive, and organisation names by the lexical rule this requirement now owns. Stage 8 imports that rule rather than keeping a second copy, and the order is fixed and stated: normalization runs before extraction, so one mention is stripped once by one rule. Where the value does not decide, nothing is decided for it (SDD-061). Stage 4 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.
features.useCase: ค่าที่ normalize แล้วยังคืนค่าดิบคู่กันเสมอ ผู้ตรวจสอบจึงเทียบรูปแบบมาตรฐานกับสิ่งที่ผู้ส่งพิมพ์มาจริงได้

features.title: Document parsing into a structured artifact that keeps its link to the raw source: a document becomes a `ParsedArtifact` carrying `document_id`, `parsed_from`, `structure`, `text_blocks`, `tables`, `metadata` and `warnings` (spec §7 plus the warnings channel the refusals below report through), where `parsed_from` is the link back to the raw artifact FR-081 stored and `metadata` records the extractor version, so a reparse after a parser change is distinguishable from the original. This closes a gap that made the stages above it unreachable: `chunkDocument` (FR-112) consumes `blocks` and, before this, nothing in `src/` produced that shape — every caller was a test, so Stages 7 and 8 were two modules with no upstream. Parsing is deterministic and refuses structure that is not there: a `#` inside a fenced or indented code block is not a heading, `#hashtag` without a space is prose, a run of dashes with no text above it is a thematic break rather than a setext heading, a sentence containing a pipe is not a table, and a table whose separator disagrees with its header is reported and left as prose rather than read with a column dropped or invented. Markdown and plain text only; the formats needing a model or a binary keep arriving through FR-071's intake contract. Stage 2 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.
features.useCase: เอกสารดิบถูก parse เป็น artifact ที่มีโครงสร้าง ตาราง และ warning พร้อมลิงก์กลับไปยังไฟล์ต้นทางที่เก็บไว้

features.title: Derived-object provenance and the lineage chain back to a source: a knowledge object carries the ten fields §8 requires of anything that came from a source — `source_id`, `source_type`, `source_uri`, `source_version`, `artifact_id`, `ingested_at`, `parsed_at`, `pipeline_version`, `extractor_version`, `checksum` — and a derived object additionally names its `derivation_method` and the `source_objects` it came from, so the chain Fact → Chunk → ParsedArtifact → RawArtifact → Source can be walked and either reaches a source or says plainly that it did not. **This carries and validates a chain of identifiers it does not mint**: identity is established by FR-071's execution ledger and by Stage 2, and FR-116 consumes it — the moment it generated a `doc_id` it would have crossed into FR-071's subject rather than sitting beside it. The contract arrives after the field did: FR-112 and FR-113 have been passing a `provenance` object between them that nothing defined and nothing checked, and Stage 2 (FR-115) hands them one, and this is what gives that blob a meaning. Nothing is defaulted, an empty provenance is refused as loudly as an absent one, and an artifact parsed before it was ingested is refused because that order cannot have happened. Stage 3 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.
features.useCase: ผู้ตรวจสอบไล่สายจากคำตอบกลับไปถึงแหล่งที่มา รุ่นของ pipeline และ checksum ของ artifact ต้นทางได้ครบสาย

features.title: Deduplication and version relationships within one tenant: an artifact is placed against the ones already held as a `DUPLICATE_OF`, a `REVISION_OF`, or independent of all of them, using BR-021's four-part ingestion identity — source identity, source version, content hash and pipeline version — computed inside a tenant and never across one (SEC-021). Both rules have carried no code anchor since they were declared; this is what gives them one. A revision emits its supersession as a PAIR, `SUPERSEDES` from the incoming artifact and `SUPERSEDED_BY` back to the one it replaced, because a graph carrying only the forward edge cannot answer "what replaced this?" from the side that was replaced, which is the side that gets asked. A duplicate emits no edge, having replaced nothing. A reparse under a changed pipeline version is a revision rather than a duplicate even when every byte matches, which is what makes reprocessing a whole corpus safe after a parser change. Nothing is defaulted: a missing component of the key is refused rather than hashed as an empty string, because a hole in a key is not an absence but a value every other artifact missing that part will collide with. `DERIVED_FROM` is never assigned here — that edge is provenance and FR-116 owns it. Stage 6 is Tier 1 under ADR-050, so this executes here.
features.useCase: artifact ที่นำเข้าซ้ำถูกจัดเป็นฉบับซ้ำหรือฉบับแก้ไขของเดิมภายใน Tenant เดียวกัน ไม่ใช่สร้างรายการใหม่ทุกครั้ง

features.title: Tier 1 stage composition: `runKnowledgeIngestionStages` calls the seven Tier 1 knowledge-ingestion stages — parsing (FR-115), provenance capture (FR-116), normalization (FR-114), classification (FR-111), deduplication (FR-117), chunking (FR-112), entity extraction (FR-113) — in ADR-050 D2's own order, over one artifact, in one call. Every prior slice in this lane shipped one calculator and a seam test to its one neighbour — parsing into chunking, chunking into entity extraction, classification into chunking, dedup into the FR-109 run input — four pairs, and a chain of pairs is not a chain, which the knowledge charter now states outright. This is the composition: proven by a test that runs all seven on one real artifact carrying a Thai organisation mention, a structured field and a structured record, and by three more asserting determinism (BR-021 requires the same input reprocess to the same chunk and candidate ids) and correct dedup classification (DUPLICATE_OF and REVISION_OF, not silently treated as fresh). Pure — no I/O, no persistence, no ledger write — so it closes no FR-109 acceptance criterion: AC-109.2, .4, .7 and .13 each require evidence on the FR-071 ledger, which a caller wanting it composes separately by wrapping each stage result with `recordPipelineEvent`, named here and not built. A stage's own error propagates unchanged; BR-022's quarantine vocabulary is declared and unbuilt, and catching an error with nowhere to classify it would read as handling that nothing downstream acts on.
features.useCase: ผู้ดูแลสั่งประมวลผลเอกสารหนึ่งครั้งเดียวแล้วได้ครบทั้งเจ็ด stage ของ Tier 1 ตามลำดับที่กำหนด

features.title: Per-stage failure attribution and BR-022 quarantine: a document that fails partway through the seven Tier 1 stages is quarantined with the complete failure envelope — `job_id`, `artifact_id`, `stage`, `error_code`, `error_message`, `retry_count`, `first_failed_at`, `last_failed_at`, `pipeline_version` — and classified retryable / non-retryable / review-required, rather than reported as nothing having happened. `runKnowledgeIngestionStagesWithTrace` extends FR-118's composition to catch each stage individually and report which succeeded before the one that did not, sharing every field mapping with the original throwing function (SDD-072) so neither duplicates the other. Every Tier 1 stage failure classifies `NON_RETRYABLE`: the seven stage functions are pure and deterministic, so a thrown validation error repeats identically on retry, and `REVIEW_REQUIRED` has no trigger either — an ambiguous value already declines via `canonical: null` (FR-114, SDD-061) rather than throwing, so it never reaches quarantine. `RETRYABLE`/`REVIEW_REQUIRED` stay in the vocabulary for failure modes this repository does not yet have (a network call, Tier 3/4 reporting) rather than being deleted for lack of a current trigger.
features.useCase: เอกสารที่ล้มกลาง pipeline เข้าคิว quarantine พร้อมบอกว่า stage ไหน error อะไร และควร retry หรือให้คนตรวจ

features.title: Self-serve account creation: an unauthenticated visitor creates their own `Person` and `PersonCredential` at a public `/signup` (`POST /api/auth/signup`) and continues into FR-066 at its `PROFILE` step. This closes the product's only door. FR-066 begins *"after a provider-neutral local identity/session exists"* and never says how one comes to exist; FR-067's invite is accepted as `acceptWorkspaceInvite({ token, personId: viewer.principal.id })`, so it attaches membership to somebody already authenticated and cannot admit a stranger; and the only writers of a credential are `prisma/seed.js` and FR-107's operator bootstrap, which is operator-run and refuses an existing credential (409). Nobody new can enter — which also means nobody new can be invited, because an invite needs a Person to attach to. **Signup itself confers no authority**: it creates no `PlatformGrant`, no Tenant, Business, Space or Project, and no `WorkspaceMembership`. What the new Person may do next is exactly what FR-066 already grants any profiled Person and no more — the owner path of `createOnboardingWorkspace`, which creates one `Portfolio` plus one OWNER `WorkspaceMembership` over it and, by AC-066.2, zero Organization/Tenant/Business/Space/Project rows. Signup therefore widens who can reach that path; it does not widen the path. Entry to an existing team remains FR-067's invite, and the resting state for a Person holding nothing is FR-066's Waiting Room. Signup never overwrites an existing `PersonCredential` — the same refusal FR-107 makes, for the same reason. Password validation and hashing are the FR-046/FR-104 path's `hashPassword`, called rather than copied, so a policy change cannot apply to one door and not the other; the human `PSN-` code comes from the same `uniqueHumanCode` generator (BR-002); and the session is FR-046's minting path, not a second implementation. **The caller is signed in on success** rather than returned to `/login` to retype the password they just chose, and the cookie is a browser-session cookie — signup carries no "remember me" tick, so it takes AC-046-15's default rather than opting itself into seven days. Creation writes an audit event. Identity stays provider-neutral and local: no SSO or third-party provider is in scope. **Email is an identifier here, not a channel.** This installation has no mail transport — the stated reason FR-104 has no public forgot-password — so there is no verification step and no "check your inbox" response to hide a taken address behind. A taken email therefore returns a distinguishable error instead of stranding the caller in silence. That enumeration is accepted deliberately: with no mail the alternative is a signup that fails invisibly, and learning that an address holds an account grants the learner nothing, because that account carries no scope, no capability and no membership until its holder creates a Workspace or an owner invites them. The compensating controls are the audit trail and a per-source rate limit — and that limit is **in-process and per-instance**: a fixed window held in the Node process's own memory, which resets on restart and does not span replicas. Stated rather than glossed, because a control described more strongly than it is built is worse than one described honestly. An unverified address must never be treated by any later requirement as proof of contact.
features.useCase: ผู้เยี่ยมชมสมัครบัญชีเองที่ /signup แล้วเข้าสู่ขั้นตอน Profile ต่อได้ทันที โดยไม่ต้องรอคำเชิญจากใคร

features.title: Google as a second way in, over the same `Person`: a visitor may present a Google account at `/signup` and `/login`, and the OAuth callback resolves the provider `sub` to exactly one internal `Person` through a namespaced external binding (FR-094) — a second way to prove who you are, never a second account path. Sign-in follows sign-up necessarily: a person who signed up with Google set no password, so refusing Google at `/login` would strand the account behind a credential that was never created. The account it produces grants nothing, exactly as FR-120: no `PlatformGrant`, Tenant, Business, Space, Project or `WorkspaceMembership`. **It does not satisfy FR-122** — Google supplies an address and a display name of its own choosing, and neither is the given name, family name or telephone number a Profile requires; the telephone number Google never supplies at all. An address matching an existing local account binds to that `Person` **only when Google asserts `email_verified`**; an unverified assertion is refused rather than linked, because linking on an unverified address is account takeover performed by signing up. **Declared blocked, not merely unbuilt**, and on two named things rather than on effort: this installation holds no OAuth client credential, and `ExternalIdentity` is keyed `(tenantId, provider, providerSubject)` with `tenantId` a required foreign key — which a self-serve signup deliberately does not have (FR-120 creates no Tenant), so the binding needs a tenant-less form before any of this can be written.
features.useCase: ผู้ใช้เลือกเข้าสู่ระบบด้วยบัญชี Google และถูก resolve เป็น Person เดิมคนเดียวกัน ไม่ใช่บัญชีใหม่คนละใบ

features.title: A Profile states who the person is, not just what to call them: FR-066's Profile step requires **given name, family name and telephone number**, over the display name it already collected and the optional email it already carried. Display name stops being something the person types twice — it is supplied by them or defaulted server-side from given + family name, never left empty, because `Person.displayName` is what every existing surface renders. The three new fields are stored **nullable on `Person`** and required **at the profile boundary instead**, and the distinction is load-bearing rather than a convenience: `Person` rows already exist that can never satisfy them — `prisma/seed.js`, FR-107's operator bootstrap, and above all every Person that FR-023's LINE ingest creates on first contact, which is created from a `lineUserId` and has no name or telephone number to give. A database-level requirement would make those rows unwritable and take the LINE intake surface down with it; the profile step is the only place a person states these things themselves, so it is the only place the requirement can be honestly enforced. Profile remains an identity step over `Person`, never an authorization grant (FR-066, BR-016).
features.useCase: ขั้นตอน Profile เก็บชื่อ นามสกุล และเบอร์โทรศัพท์ เพื่อให้ระบุตัวคนได้จริง ไม่ใช่แค่ชื่อที่ใช้เรียก

features.title: Plugin authentication and capability discovery: first-party Codex/Claude Code harnesses obtain authority through a server-owned authorization-code flow under `/api/plugin/auth` — a signed-in browser session authorizes a 60-second single-use code bound to an exact `client_id`, an exact registered `redirect_uri`, an `installation_id` and a PKCE S256 challenge; exchanging it with the verifier yields a 15-minute opaque bearer session. Codes and tokens are persisted as SHA-256 hashes only, so a database read recovers nothing usable. Capabilities are **derived** from `resolveViewer` and are advisory UX: reads for any visible Business, `requiresApproval` writes only where the person owns one, and every command re-authorizes on its own path before mutating anything. The plugin never submits a human password, copies the `zuri_session` cookie, uses `Mcp-Session-Id` as authorization, connects to the database, or self-asserts Tenant/Business/Membership/role scope; it also never inherits a platform DEV grant, so installing a plugin cannot widen what the person could already reach. Redirect matching is exact and stays exact — `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` are two registrations, a decision forced by a Preview transport that rewrites one into the other (ADR-052 D1). Replaying a consumed code is treated as evidence the code leaked after use: it is refused **and** revokes the session that code already minted. Revoke is idempotent and answers identically for a token that never existed. Distinct from FR-106's `ApiAccessKey`, which is a long-lived Tenant-bound service credential; this is a minutes-long delegation from one person to one installation (ADR-052). Authorization is a two-step gate: `GET /authorize` renders a consent screen and mints nothing, and only a POST from that screen's form — carrying the session cookie, a session-bound anti-CSRF token and an HMAC-signed request token whose parameters are the ones displayed — mints a code. Refusal returns `error=access_denied` with the original `state` (ADR-052 D4).
features.useCase: นักพัฒนาผูก Codex/Claude Code harness เข้ากับ installation ผ่าน authorization code อายุสั้นครั้งเดียว โดยไม่ต้องกรอกรหัสผ่านหรือคัดลอก cookie

features.title: Product Readiness: one read-only Platform surface at `/platform/product-readiness`, with a stable drilldown at `/platform/product-readiness/[domain]`, that answers four questions separately rather than collapsing them into one green number — how much evidence-backed implementation exists, which requirements are actually verified, whether a complete feature is ready to use, and what a Human can use it for. It renders the committed `docs/.domain-state.json` projection and nothing else: no database model, no runtime write path, no scheduled poll, no external API. **Readiness is not progress.** A feature is ready only when every underlying FR is verified and, for an explicit FEAT bundle, the registry says `live`; a 100% implementation score therefore still reads not-ready when the registry says `building`, and the surface always prints both numbers with the blocking reason. Progress itself is weighted 20% declaration + 40% code + 40% test — **a policy choice, not a derived fact**, held in one named constant (`PROGRESS_METHODOLOGY` in `scripts/domain-state.mjs`), printed beside the numbers in the UI and carried in the snapshot, and awaiting owner sign-off rather than inheritance. Projection is complete by construction: every FEAT bundle and every unbundled FR appears exactly once with one hand-written use case, and missing, duplicate, unknown or use-case-less metadata aborts graph generation, because a partial list is a wrong answer. The surface resolves its viewer on the server before rendering, so the snapshot never reaches an unauthorized browser through the RSC payload.
features.useCase: ผู้บริหารเปิด Product Readiness เพื่อดูความคืบหน้าของทุกโดเมน แล้ว drill down ถึง feature, ตัวอย่าง use case, หลักฐาน code/test และสิ่งที่ยังติดอยู่

features.title: FlowAccount read-only pull pipeline: an OWNER-authorized Business can onboard one FlowAccount Client Credentials connection through a provider-specific Platform wizard that accepts Client ID/Client Secret write-only, provisions them into the approved secret manager, verifies `GET /company/info`, and returns redacted metadata only. A server-owned `FLOWACCOUNT` adapter exchanges/reuses Bearer tokens, calls only the approved GET resource catalog, paginates within the provider page-size ceiling, respects provider account rate limits, and sends every record through the existing FR-081 `zIngestionEnvelope`/`RawExternalRecord` path with trusted Tenant/Business/connection scope, external identity, payload hash, IngestionRun, SyncCursor and DeadLetterRecord evidence. Cursor advancement requires a complete resource run; document incrementals use a lookback window and master resources use full hash reconciliation because FlowAccount exposes no generic updated-since cursor. The UI exposes computed data-source health and run summaries, never raw secret/token/payload. Public OpenAPI evidence is not GL/TB/P&L or Accounting truth; provider writes, OpenID, webhook, scheduler and downstream domain publication are separate future requirements. Design is ADR-053
features.useCase: Owner เชื่อม FlowAccount ของ Business ผ่าน wizard ที่รับ Client ID/Secret แบบเขียนอย่างเดียว แล้วดึงข้อมูลบัญชีแบบอ่านอย่างเดียวโดยไม่เปิดเผย secret กลับมาที่ browser

features.title: Catalog publication approval gate: a `DPL-SUPABASE-BUSINESS-KNOWLEDGE-V1` run that has produced a candidate projection does not reach `DPS-PUBLISH` until an authorized human has recorded an `APPROVED` `PipelineGateDecision` against that run, and a `REJECTED` decision sends it to `DPS-ROLLBACK` instead — the two stage labels FR-071's catalog has always carried ("Publish approved projection", "Rollback failed or rejected run") with nothing yet deciding which one a run takes. (a) The decision is recorded on the existing FR-071 execution ledger and declares **no new model and no new column**: `PipelineGateDecision.decidedByPersonId` is who signed, that row's own `createdAt` is when, `required` is whether the gate was waivable, `reason` carries a rejection, and `PipelineRun.artifactRef`/`artifactSha256` already identify the artifact the run applied. A second run table as CR-003 proposes is refused: `IngestionRun` (FR-081) is acquisition evidence for one connection and `PipelineRun` (FR-071) is the execution ledger for one pipeline definition, and a third answer to "what happened in this pipeline" would make the reconciliation evidence something that has to be believed twice (SDD-057). (b) The evidence a reviewer acted on — the candidate publication's own identity, and the added/changed/unchanged counts shown — is written to `PipelineGateDecision.evidenceJson` (SDD-075); a signature whose evidence is empty records that somebody approved but not what they saw, which is not an auditable decision. (c) The destination vault is not stored: it resolves from the run's Tenant/Business scope through API-010 (FR-057, ADR-022), so a stored copy would be a second answer to which vault a scope maps to. (d) Tier 1 records and does not execute (ADR-043 D2.1, ADR-050 D3). The gate is therefore a precondition the executing worker must observe and the ledger makes checkable afterwards — a run whose publish stage succeeded with no prior `APPROVED` decision is a detectable violation — not an interlock this repository enforces on a worker it does not run. (e) **Distinct from FR-110's Stage 17 quality gate**, permanently and by design: FR-110 is an automated `PASS`/`PASS_WITH_WARNINGS` verdict on a `DPL-KNOWLEDGE-INGEST-V1` knowledge snapshot, this is a human signature on a business-knowledge catalog version, and both will answer to "approval gate on a pipeline run" in any future search while sharing the one `PipelineGateDecision` table. Reworked from CR-003; no reviewer UI is in scope (CR-003 §2.B is a feature programme, not this requirement)
features.useCase: ผู้มีอำนาจอนุมัติตรวจ catalog version ที่ยังไม่เผยแพร่พร้อมยอดที่เพิ่ม เปลี่ยน และไม่เปลี่ยน แล้วลงชื่ออนุมัติหรือปฏิเสธ โดยลายเซ็นและหลักฐานที่เห็นถูกบันทึกไว้กับ run เดียวกัน

features.title: Business-scoped GitHub repository projection: a `Repository` a Business already owns may additionally name its GitHub origin, and a person the Business admits may read that repository's tree and file contents in the console, read-only. (a) The binding declares **no new model, no new column and no migration**, because the entity already exists: FR-008 created `Repository` and FR-073 made it owned by exactly one Business, which is the scope CR-004 also chose and the only scope the viewer contract can govern (SDD-037). CR-004's `githubRepoUrl` is `Repository.url` beside `ownerName`/`repoName`/`fullName`/`provider`; its `githubBranch` is `Repository.defaultBranch`, with `ProjectRepository.branch` as the per-link override; GitHub's numeric repository id is `Repository.externalRepoId` mapped through `ExternalEntityRef` — the identifier BR-002 names by example ("GitHub id") and forbids as a key; and CR-004's three sync fields are **not stored at all**, because they are artifacts of a design this one does not adopt: `lastCommitSha`, `lastGithubSyncAt` and `githubSyncStatus` describe a mirror kept in step with an origin, and a read-through projection (d) keeps no mirror — the commit a reader is looking at comes from the same live fetch that produced the tree, so storing it would be a second answer to a question the response already carries. Should a cache ever be added, the watermark is `SyncCursor.cursorValue` with `lastSuccessAt` beside it and `IngestionRun.status` for the outcome, and that is the point at which its keying must be settled rather than assumed: `SyncCursor` is unique on `(connectionId, resourceType)`, so one connection covering several repositories has no per-repository cursor without either compounding `resourceType` or narrowing a connection to one repository — and `externalAccountId` names an *account*, which is why `Repository` is a separate model in the first place. Five columns on `Business` are refused: `Business` is a scope-chain entity, columns on it would cap a Business at one repository where `Repository` already permits many, and a foreign URL and commit SHA on a core scope row is the shape BR-002 exists to prevent. (b) A private repository's credential is an `IntegrationCredential.secretRef` on a `github` `IntegrationConnection`, resolved through the `SecretManagerPort` — a reference, never material, never in a browser response (SDD-043, SEC-015). Registering the provider row is idempotent on its code and needs no migration. (c) Push delivery is an **FR-081 adapter, not a new endpoint**: a webhook is one of the four `SOURCE_TYPES` that requirement already names, and a bespoke `/api/webhooks/github` would be the second raw-write path FR-081 forbids by name — the same finding CR-005's LINE connector drew. The tenant CR-004 omits is never read from the payload: the delivery's `installation.id` selects exactly one `IntegrationConnection` on `(providerId, externalAccountId)` and **zero or multiple candidates fail closed** (the FR-079 rule), the connection carries the trusted `tenantId`/`businessId`, and `repository.id` then resolves to a `Repository` through `ExternalEntityRef`. The authentication CR-004 omits is GitHub's `X-Hub-Signature-256` — HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body under the connection's webhook secret, constant-time compared, verified before anything is parsed for meaning or written; routing reads `installation.id` only, which is a non-secret selector the signature then proves, so trust follows verification rather than preceding it. (d) **File content is never persisted** — only push metadata converges on the raw substrate, and the tree and blob reads that render a file are read-through with no row of their own (SDD-076). Writes to `Repository` continue to go through project-manager's `repository-service`, which stays its only writer; this requirement reads that model and does not claim it. (e) The projection is bounded by a declared path scope, deny-by-default in the shape SEC-009 already uses, and `vaults/`-class live database state is excluded rather than discovered by a previewer (CR-006 §5.2). No file tree UI, purpose badge, multi-format previewer or metadata panel is in scope: CR-004 §2.B is a four-part feature programme, not this requirement. Reworked from CR-004
features.useCase: Owner ผูก repository GitHub เข้ากับ Business ที่ตนดูแล แล้วเปิดอ่านโครงสร้างไฟล์และเนื้อไฟล์ในคอนโซลแบบอ่านอย่างเดียว เฉพาะ path ที่ประกาศไว้ โดยระบบไม่เก็บสำเนาเนื้อไฟล์ไว้เลย

features.title: Shipping rate card as governed business knowledge: a Business's logistics rate matrix — Member tier × warehouse × shipping method × category, each cell a THB/CBM rate and a THB/kg rate with the CBM and weight minima that qualify a shipment for that tier — is published as `business_knowledge` rows under a **second `knowledge_type`**, and declares **no Prisma model, no new domain and no settings write path**. (a) The rows go where the same Business's product prices already go. `zuri_core.business_knowledge` is Tenant- and Business-scoped under forced RLS behind a `SET LOCAL ROLE` login (SDD-026) and already carries every fact a rate needs: `as_of` for the sheet's effective date, `approved_at`, `source_ref` and `source_sha256` for the supplier rate sheet the numbers came from, `is_active` for supersession, plus `unit`, `sell_price` and a `specification` object for the per-kilogram rate and the tier minima. CR-005's `ShippingRateMatrix` Prisma model is refused for the reason SDD-077 gives, and additionally because no chartered domain may hold it: `knowledge` owns no Prisma models by design and has kept that boundary through FR-109…FR-119, and `market-intelligence` reserves commercial state for a "Commerce authority" that has no charter in this repository. (b) Rates enter through the intake already built for this exact input. The sheets are supplier documents, so `SMARTGIFT_DOCUMENT_INTAKE` stages them (`document-intake-contract.js` accepts image sources), `DPL-SUPABASE-BUSINESS-KNOWLEDGE-V1` publishes them, and FR-129's `APPROVED` `PipelineGateDecision` is what makes a rate change readable. The administrator-editable grid of CR-005 §3.B.1 is refused on that ground rather than on effort: a rate a person may silently retype has no effective date, no signature and no source, and a quotation priced from it cannot be explained afterwards. (c) The density switch — charge by weight at or above 400 kg/CBM, by volume below — is a property of the published card, not of a cell, and is carried once per version rather than copied onto every cell, where sixty-four copies are sixty-four chances to disagree. (d) **Sell-side only.** FR-047 excludes cost and margin from this projection by name; what a customer is charged belongs here and the cost basis behind CR-005 §4.1's margin floor does not (FR-132 (c)). (e) Scope is `(tenant_id, business_id)` and not the `workspaceId` CR-005 proposes: `Workspace.tenantId` and `Workspace.businessId` are both nullable under `scopeType` `PORTFOLIO`/`TENANT`/`BUSINESS`, and a LINE turn resolves `{tenantId, businessId}` from its server-owned binding (FR-052) and never holds a `workspaceId` at all, so a workspace-keyed rate is unreadable from the one surface that needs it. Reworked from CR-005; the quoting behaviour is FR-132
features.useCase: ผู้ดูแลนำเข้าใบอัตราค่าขนส่งของซัพพลายเออร์เป็นเอกสาร แล้วอัตราตามระดับสมาชิกถูกเผยแพร่เป็น business knowledge ที่บอกได้ว่ามีผลเมื่อใด ใครอนุมัติ และมาจากไฟล์ต้นทางใด ไม่ใช่ตารางที่แก้ทับได้เงียบ ๆ

features.title: Ladder quotation on the LINE surface, as a Gate E read-only tool: a customer asking for a price inside an existing LINE conversation ("ขอใบเสนอราคา", "คำนวณราคา TDD03-2 จำนวน 100 ชิ้น") gets a tiered quotation in the reply, and this declares **no route, no model, no converter and no credential**. (a) It adds nothing to the intake path because that path is already complete. The FR-028 webhook receives an already-verified, already-normalized batch from `zuri.command-agent`; `normalizeLineWebhookEvent` already converts every event onto the FR-081 ingestion envelope; `handleAgentTurn` already runs the turn. CR-005's `/api/connectors/line-oa/[businessId]` is refused as the second write path BR-009 and SDD-009 forbid by name — and so is the *converter* a first reading of that refusal implies, because the converter exists and has since FR-081. What is missing is one descriptor in `defaultReadOnlyTools`, which registers cleanly at Gate E precisely because a quotation computes and writes nothing (`createToolRegistry` rejects any descriptor whose `readOnly` is not `true`). (b) The reply is **returned** to the sole transport owner, never sent: BR-011 gives `zuri.command-agent` signature verification and the Reply API, and FR-050 gives this repository at most one reply text per event and no `replyToken`. The LINE Flex Message of CR-005 §3.B.2 is therefore the transport's rendering of the answer this repository returns, not something this repository posts — the boundary FR-128 already keeps for the Daily Sales Brief. (c) CR-005 §4's two invariants are both kept, and split by who may see them: rounding up to the nearest 10 THB is part of the quoted number and belongs in the reply, while the margin floor is a cost-side test applied before the number is returned and never carried in the payload, because FR-047 excludes margin from what this surface may read. A quotation that showed its own floor would breach that exclusion in the one place a customer is reading. (d) Authorization is the registry's own: `requireToolAuthorization` resolves `{tenantId, businessId, principalId}` from the turn's AuthContext and calls `authorizeScope`, so a quote is priced from the asking Business's rate card and from no other. (e) An MCP tool as CR-005 §3.B.3 proposes is a **different surface, not this one**, and is neither refused nor part of this requirement: `/api/mcp` is a viewer-authenticated back-office transport whose registry (`TOOL_DEFINITIONS`) shares no code with the in-process Gate E registry a LINE turn binds. Reworked from CR-005
features.useCase: ลูกค้าถามราคาในห้องแชท LINE เดิม แล้วได้ใบเสนอราคาแบบขั้นบันไดที่ปัดขึ้นเป็นสิบบาทกลับไปในคำตอบ โดยกำไรขั้นต่ำถูกบังคับก่อนตอบและไม่ถูกส่งออกไปกับราคา

features.title: Edge Device heartbeat registry — the cloud-side liveness view ADR-041 D3 promises the console, and nothing more: `GET`, `POST` and `DELETE /api/agent/heartbeat` each resolve one trusted viewer before any work and fail closed (a missing or invalid session is 401, never an anonymous device list). A heartbeat is a validated `{businessId, deviceId, status, contractVersion, registeredQueries, approvedTemplates, engine?, model?}` payload: a failed parse is 400 carrying the issues and registers nothing (there is no default device), and `businessId` must be a Business the viewer **owns** (`ownsBusiness`, 403 otherwise). The registry is keyed by `(businessId, deviceId)`; a viewer lists and removes only devices of Businesses they own, and `DELETE` without `deviceId` clears exactly that owned scope. `deviceToken` is accepted on the wire for compatibility and is never stored, returned or audited (ADR-041 D3: zero edge secrets in the cloud). A device is `online` when its last heartbeat is within 120 s and its status is `healthy`. First registration, every status transition and every removal write an `EDGE_DEVICE` audit event; a tick that changes nothing writes none. Every failure returns its real status code through the shared `handle` helper. Liveness lives in a process-local registry **by decision**: the agent charter owns no Prisma model, a heartbeat is a cache that goes stale in two minutes rather than a record, and the cost is stated rather than hidden — the registry is empty after a cold start and is per-instance on Vercel, so the console reads "not paired" until the next tick reaches the instance that serves it. Durable pairing (a device record with a token reference) is a separate declaration this FR does not make.
features.useCase: เจ้าของธุรกิจเปิดหน้า Platform Integrations แล้วเห็นว่า Edge Device ของธุรกิจตนออนไลน์อยู่หรือไม่จากสัญญาณ heartbeat ล่าสุด และถอดอุปกรณ์ออกได้เฉพาะของธุรกิจที่ตนเป็นเจ้าของ ผู้ที่ไม่มี session ถูกปฏิเสธทุกคำขอ และ token ของอุปกรณ์ไม่ถูกเก็บไว้บนคลาวด์

features.title: Deployment liveness probe and public-origin abstraction (ADR-058): `GET /api/health` answers without a session, runs exactly one trivial query (`SELECT 1`) against the configured application database, and returns `{status:'ok', db:'ok'}` with 200 or `{status:'degraded', db:'unreachable'}` with 503 — states, counts and timings only, never an error message, host or credential (SEC-009). It is the probe Docker Compose uses to mark the `web` container healthy and to start ngrok only after it. The deployment's public origin is one run-time variable, `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (`src/lib/public-base-url.js`: `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` → build-time `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` → `http://localhost:3100`, reduced to an origin; a non-HTTP or unparsable value is ignored, not propagated); the root layout's `metadataBase` and the Platform Integrations pairing payload and LINE webhook URL derive from it or from the origin the page was actually served from — no platform hostname is assumed anywhere.
features.useCase: ผู้ดูแลระบบรัน docker compose up -d บนเครื่องของตนเอง แล้ว Compose รู้เองว่า web พร้อมให้บริการจาก GET /api/health ก่อนจะเปิด ngrok ออกสู่อินเทอร์เน็ต และหน้า Platform Integrations แสดง webhook URL จาก origin ที่เปิดอยู่จริง (https://<NGROK_DOMAIN>/api/agent/line-webhook) โดยไม่ต้องพึ่ง Vercel

features.title: Supabase pooler MODE follows deployment topology, not a fixed default (ADR-058 D9): `resolvePoolMode(env)` (`src/lib/db.js`) picks Supavisor SESSION pooling (port 5432, no `pgbouncer` param) for a long-running process and TRANSACTION pooling (port 6543, `pgbouncer=true`) only when `VERCEL` is set, so a single container gets a small stable connection count and one Postgres round trip per query instead of paying a transaction-mode backend checkout on every query it never needed; `ZURI_DB_POOL_MODE=session|transaction` is an explicit operator override for a topology neither branch guesses (e.g. several container replicas sharing one Postgres, which still needs transaction-mode safety). Applies only to a `*.pooler.supabase.com` host — a direct connection or non-Supabase Postgres passes through untouched.
features.useCase: ผู้ดูแลระบบรัน docker compose up -d แล้ว query ทุกตัวไปหา Supabase ผ่าน session pooling ที่เร็วเป็นค่า default โดยไม่ต้องตั้งค่าอะไรเพิ่ม เพราะระบบรู้เองว่าตัวเองรันเป็น container เดียวยาว ๆ ไม่ใช่ serverless function บน Vercel

features.title: Supply-chain navigation groups its four modules under one SCM slot (ADR-069) — `DOMAIN_GROUPS` declares `scm` over the existing `inventory`, `warehouse`, `procurement` and `commerce` domains, the bar renders one slot for the group and the sidebar lists the whole group with each child's label heading its own pages, so a child reached from the bar can reach its siblings. The group is a container and never a grant: `scm` is absent from the registry, so it cannot reach `Membership.domainKeysJson`, the permission checkboxes or the route guard, which keeps resolving a path to the leaf domain and asking about that key (FR-061 unchanged). The `inventory` lane is labelled Inventory again and `commerce` is labelled Order Management, both route keys unchanged; `warehouse` is a reserved sibling for locations, transfers and stocktake, listed and disabled until it is built.
features.useCase: ผู้ใช้กดช่อง SCM ช่องเดียวในแถบโดเมน แล้วเห็น Inventory, Warehouse, Procurement และ Order Management เรียงเป็นสี่กลุ่มในเมนูด้านซ้าย จึงข้ามจากคลังไปจัดซื้อไปคำสั่งขายได้โดยไม่ต้องกลับขึ้นแถบบน ส่วน Warehouse ที่ยังไม่ได้สร้างจะแสดงเป็นช่องที่กดไม่ได้ แทนที่จะหายไปเฉย ๆ

features.title: A product declares one of three natures, and they differ in accounting rather than in bookkeeping convenience — `stockPolicy` is TRACKED (สินค้านับสต๊อก: a good the Business counts, every movement a ledger row, cost held in stock until the goods leave), UNTRACKED (สินค้าไม่นับสต๊อก: still a good, still buyable and receivable, but carrying no perpetual count, so no on-hand at all rather than a zero) or SERVICE (บริการ: not a good, so no stock fields exist, `movementRule` refuses it by its own code `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_IS_A_SERVICE`, and a goods receipt naming it is refused with `PROCUREMENT_RECEIPT_LINE_IS_A_SERVICE` because a service is performed, not delivered). Anything without a ledger is stored with `trackingMode` NONE, so neither an uncounted good nor a service can ask for lot or serial identity it can never have. The catalogue form narrows to the nature chosen: picking ไม่นับสต๊อก or บริการ removes the tracking mode and safety-stock fields instead of leaving fields that cannot apply.
features.useCase: เจ้าของธุรกิจสร้าง SKU แล้วเลือกได้ว่าเป็นสินค้านับสต๊อก สินค้าไม่นับสต๊อก หรือบริการ พอเลือกบริการหรือไม่นับสต๊อก ฟอร์มจะตัดช่องการระบุหน่วยและ safety stock ออกทันทีเพราะใช้ไม่ได้ และระบบจะปฏิเสธการรับของเข้าคลังสำหรับบริการ เพราะบริการเป็นสิ่งที่ทำให้ ไม่ใช่ของที่ส่งมอบเข้าคลัง

features.title: A Business declares feature capabilities (`Business.capabilitiesJson`), distinct from a Membership grant — a grant says who may open a module the Business already has, a capability says whether the module applies to the Business at all. The first capability is `physicalStock` (default on, so every Business with existing Inventory data is unaffected): when a Business turns it off, the reserved Warehouse slot (`key: warehouse`, ADR-069 D3) is hidden from the domain bar and the SCM sidebar entirely, not merely disabled — `domainBarSlots`/`sidebarDomainForPath` read it from the same Business object the bar and sidebar already hold, so the two can never disagree. `PATCH /api/businesses/[id]/capabilities` is the only writer, OWNER-scoped, expected-version compare-and-set, one AuditEvent per toggle; every reader is `/api/scope`, which already returns every Business column.
features.useCase: เจ้าของธุรกิจที่ขายเฉพาะบริการเข้าไปที่ตั้งค่า แล้วปิดสวิตช์ Physical Stock ทันทีที่ปิด โมดูล Warehouse หายไปจากแถบเมนูบนและเมนูซ้ายของ SCM ทั้งหมด ไม่ใช่แค่กดไม่ได้ ธุรกิจอื่นที่มีสต๊อกจริงยังเห็น Warehouse เหมือนเดิมเพราะค่าเริ่มต้นเปิดไว้

features.title: A sub-domain module with more than one page renders them as tabs inside its own canvas (`<ModuleTabs>`, `src/lib/module-tabs.js`), not only as separate sidebar entries — the owner's instruction that a module's views live in the canvas and switch by clicking a tab. Each tab is a normal client-navigated route, not query-param or component state: the active tab is derived from `usePathname()`, the same id-binding idiom `DomainBar` and `Sidebar` already use for their own active-state checks. No route moves — Procurement (Dashboard, Purchase Orders) and Order Management/Commerce (Dashboard, Orders) keep exactly the URLs FR-164/FR-166 declared, so no existing e2e assertion changes.
features.useCase: ผู้ใช้เปิดหน้าจัดซื้อแล้วเห็นแท็บ Dashboard กับ Purchase Orders อยู่ในกรอบเดียวกันด้านบน กดสลับแท็บเพื่อดูใบสั่งซื้อโดยไม่ต้องกลับไปที่เมนูซ้าย เช่นเดียวกับหน้า Order Management ที่มีแท็บ Dashboard กับ Orders สลับกันได้ในกรอบเดียว

features.title: Execution Trace & Replay v0.3 — the agent domain owns one scoped append-only `AgentTraceEvent` journal for the native SERVER LINE path. It records one event per actual turn input, model call, tool/action invocation, retrieval, memory or delivery observation, separating UUID `turnId`/`executionId`/`instanceId`/opaque MSP `sessionId`/`ctxId` from stable tool registry/action-intent ids, fresh model/tool/action/send attempt ids, document/artifact versions, retrieval/memory references and delivery receipts. Runtime instanceId is process-stable; executionId changes per claimed attempt. It reuses `LineConversationJob.id` as `turnId`, stores exact semantic input snapshots up to 1 MiB plus SHA-256 and explicit retention/redaction states, keeps provider usage subsets, timestamps and recipient evidence nullable/truthful in UTC, and returns owner-only, `line-oa`-visible read-only playback at `GET /api/line-oa/jobs/{id}/trace`; missing retention makes playback `REPLAY_INCOMPLETE`, and playback performs no effects. Native SERVER defaults to no private memory adapter: jobs without the approved immutable per-job opt-in retain empty memory refs plus `EXCLUDED_BY_POLICY`, while opted-in worker jobs may compose the trusted MSP thread adapter and durable local receipt checkpoint. MSP Soul/session/memory authority, GKS retrieval and optional Edge adapters remain separate external gates and receive no direct foreign DB writes.
features.useCase: Inspect exact context, model usage and delivery evidence for a native SERVER LINE turn without repeating side effects.

features.title: Customer-facing navigation groups two domains under one CRM slot (ADR-071), extending the ADR-069 precedent to the rest of the bar — `DOMAIN_GROUPS` gains a second entry, `crm`, over the existing `customer` and `market` domains; the bar renders one slot for the group and the sidebar lists both, each child's label heading its own pages. The group is a container and never a grant, exactly as `scm` is not: `crm` is absent from the registry, so it cannot reach `Membership.domainKeysJson`, the permission checkboxes or the route guard, which keeps resolving a path to the leaf domain and asking about that key (FR-061 unchanged). The `customer` lane is relabelled from "CRM" to "Customer" so the leaf and the new group do not both read "CRM"; `market` keeps its label and its key. Every other remaining bar domain — Marketing, Operations, HR/People, Development, Asset Management, LINE OA Studio, Platform — is confirmed unchanged: each already stands as one complete ERP-recognised module with no sibling to consolidate (ADR-071's Context table records the check for each). Renumbered from FR-171/ADR-070 — main's Execution Trace & Replay v0.3 already held those ids when this branch rebased.
features.useCase: ผู้ใช้กดช่อง CRM ช่องเดียวในแถบโดเมน แล้วเห็น Customer กับ Market Intelligence เรียงกันในเมนูด้านซ้าย จึงข้ามจากลูกค้าไปข้อมูลตลาดได้โดยไม่ต้องกลับขึ้นแถบบน เหมือนกับที่ SCM ทำไว้กับคลัง จัดซื้อ และคำสั่งขาย

features.title: Atomic POS checkout composes existing Commerce orders, pending payments and Inventory — `POST /api/commerce/pos/checkout` validates an authorized Business, selected active Branch and selected active WarehouseLocation, `WALK_IN` order lines with manually supplied FR-166 `unitPrice`, exact integer-satang totals and the existing `QR`, `CASH`, `TRANSFER`, `CARD` and `OTHER` payment vocabulary. One transaction creates the `SalesOrder`, records a `PENDING` `Payment`, issues tracked stock through Inventory's exported `appendMovement` with its own authority and returns exact cash change; a separate existing FR-163 verifier is the only path to `VERIFIED` money. Invalid line/product/customer scope, missing location, insufficient cash, duplicate reference, inventory shortage, lot/serial refusal or any later audit failure rolls back every row. `GET /api/commerce/pos/catalogue` exposes same-Business active product identity and recomputed stock without deriving a price from inventory cost or a fallback. A terminal label is request/receipt metadata only; P3 introduces no persistent terminal registry or default station.
features.useCase: An authorized cashier submits a manually priced walk-in sale for a selected Branch and WarehouseLocation, and one transaction records the order, pending payment, exact change and Inventory ledger issue without claiming verification

features.title: Business-scoped durable Commerce document issuance and issuer/tax/PromptPay configuration — `CommerceDocument` is an immutable snapshot linked to one Business, sales order and selected active Branch, with closed types `INVOICE`, `RECEIPT`, `TAX_INVOICE` and `ABB_TAX_INVOICE`. `POST /api/commerce/billing/documents/preview` validates scope, configured issuer/tax/recipient policy and buyer `ISSUANCE_INPUT` without persisting a number, issued timestamp or audit event; `POST /api/commerce/billing/documents` performs transactional issuance with one immutable snapshot, one audit event, a retry-safe idempotency key and an atomic per-Business/type/calendar-year sequence. Seller identity comes from the Business's LegalEntity, verified Thai identifier and configured legal/Branch address; a Business OWNER edits issuer, versioned VAT, PromptPay, non-VAT and walk-in policy through the settings flow, and missing/inactive/unverified values remain explicitly unavailable. VAT issue requires the configured effective, verified policy; durable `RECEIPT` issue requires verified payment at least equal to document gross, while preview may show unpaid or pending state without claiming receipt. P3 uses document-level `ROUND_HALF_UP` integer-satang VAT, requires `nonVatDocumentPolicy = ALLOW_INVOICE_RECEIPT` for non-VAT invoice/receipt and `walkInDocumentPolicy = ALLOW_ANONYMOUS_RECEIPT` for receipt-only anonymous walk-in; full tax documents require validated buyer issuance input. Billing accepts only the existing FR-166 `THB` order currency in this slice; unsupported currencies fail before preview or issue with no FX conversion. PromptPay is the existing `Payment.method = QR` with a Business-scoped configured, active, verified recipient; the local EMVCo/Thai QR payload is not bank or statutory evidence. No void/correction route, CRM write, terminal registry, price catalogue, live provider call or production activation is part of this requirement.
features.useCase: Business owner configures authoritative issuer, tax and PromptPay settings, then an authorized user previews or durably issues an immutable invoice, receipt or Thai tax document with an exact money snapshot and no fabricated identity

features.title: Server-owned LINE transport reports its own reachability, so a silent channel is visible instead of inferred — for every LineOaAccount with serverEnabled the server derives the age of the last inbound delivery it recorded (from existing Integration evidence and LineConversationJob rows; no new column, no migration) and classifies it OK, QUIET or SILENT against configurable thresholds, and separately asks LINE for the channel configured webhook endpoint and compares it with this deployment own account route, classifying MATCHED, MISMATCHED, DISABLED or UNKNOWN. GET /api/line-oa/accounts/{id}/transport-health answers states, timestamps and durations only — never channel credentials and never the other endpoint contents — the LINE OA console shows the state beside the account, and the existing server worker tick logs one structured warning per account while a state is not OK. Read-only: no writes, no new process, and no automatic change to provider configuration.
features.useCase: Tell a silent LINE channel from a misrouted one: how long a serverEnabled account has gone without an inbound delivery, and whether the webhook endpoint LINE has configured is still this deployment own account route.
